content:
Andre Albuquerque went from zero coding ability to outshipping engineering teams using five AI agents inside Claude Code. Each one mirrors a real squad member: researcher, discovery, designer, engineer, implementer. A PM orchestrator sits on top and routes every task without writing a single line of code itself.

His CLAUDE.md is what makes the whole system hold together. Andre calls it "the values of your Claude." Every rule, every constraint, every architecture decision loads before a single task runs. His first rule: always call the PM agent. The PM agent never builds. It decides which specialist agent handles the work. Exactly how a real PM operates inside a squad.

Here's where it gets interesting. When a feature ships broken, Andre doesn't fix the feature. He fixes the agent that built it, updates the CLAUDE.md constraint, then runs the entire pipeline again from scratch. Same failure never happens twice. Every fix multiplies across every future feature because the infrastructure remembers.

50% of his build time goes into improving agent infrastructure rather than shipping features. That ratio sounds backwards until you see the compounding. Three people running this setup now match the output of teams running 15. The gap widens every week because each infrastructure improvement accelerates every task that follows it.

The collaboration insight from this episode is the one most teams will resist. Andre argues execution should be solo. Discovery and delivery should be collaborative. Most companies have it completely inverted: PMs decide alone, then everyone collaborates on execution through dependencies and handoffs and blockers. Flip that and every person on the squad becomes a builder who can ship independently.

This is using a project named Envoy.

In summary, you can connect any number of agents to a shared space and have them collaborate with one another.

Envoy acts as a shared context layer across all of your agents, sessions, and computers.

Imagine you connect Claude Code, Codex, and a Code Review agent to a shared Envoy space.

Claude Code reviews a pull request and posts the list of issues it found. Codex claims two of those issues, fixes them, and posts the results. The Code Review agent is watching the space and automatically reviews every fix.

All of this happens without needing to write any code or use API keys. You need one binary file (Envoy) and an invite code to connect any agent to the space.

The impressive part here is the protocol that sits under all of this: Statecraft.

If you want to try it, the local version is completely free. Here is the link to the GitHub repository:

As a full-stack AI capabilities provider, Alibaba is well-positioned to access a market opportunity poised for exponential growth. Against this backdrop, our AI business has moved beyond its initial investment phase and has officially entered a period of commercial returns. Driven by robust AI demand, external commercial revenue from Cloud Intelligence Group accelerated to 40% year-over-year growth in the final quarter of this fiscal year, with AI-related revenue accounting for 30% of the total. AI is now powering a comprehensive upgrade across all Alibaba Cloud businesses, shifting the primary growth engine from traditional computing and storage toward models, computing power, and agent-based services.

At the AI infrastructure layer, our self-developed Pingtouge AI chips have achieved mass production, delivering high-quality computing power to support cloud infrastructure and our MaaS (Model-as-a-Service) inference platform. On the foundation model front, our R&D pace has significantly accelerated: the Qwen large model has undergone three stable iterations in the past three months. The latest iteration, Qwen3.7-Max, is purpose-built for AI agents and delivers continuous breakthroughs in core capabilities such as coding and reasoning. To complement the Qwen model family, we are also accelerating our deployment of specialized models, including HappyOyster—an open-world model designed for real-time interactive creation—and HappyHorse, a multimodal model focused on cross-modal understanding and generation.

At the application layer, in November 2025, we launched the Qwen App—a versatile personal AI assistant for consumers that integrates life, work, and learning functionalities. The Qwen App is deeply interconnected with various applications across our ecosystem, including Taobao, Tmall, Taobao Flash Delivery, Fliggy, Damai, Amap, and Alipay—giving it unique advantages in everyday life, services, productivity, and entertainment. These broader integrations expand user reach, enhance engagement between Alibaba’s ecosystem and external services, and reinforce our leadership in applied AI. We have also introduced Wukong, an enterprise-grade, AI-native workspace for business users, which leverages AI agents to manage complex workflows and connects to skill modules built upon Alibaba’s ecosystem. Together, Wukong and the Qwen App form our dual-pronged AI application strategy targeting both enterprise and consumer markets.

With full-stack capabilities across the AI value chain, Alibaba holds a strategic advantage in this new AI era. Backed by deep reserves of talent, technology, and resources, we are confident in our ability to seize this generational opportunity and establish AI + Cloud as another major growth engine for Alibaba. We see tremendous value and opportunity in this evolving market.

Taobao and Tmall will continue to prioritize user growth and experience enhancement. We must stay ahead of user needs and remain agile in a rapidly evolving market to win in competition.

つくる過程も、
受注から納品までの過程も、
話題になるめちゃくちゃ『個性的』な人。

スキル云々ではなくて
『らしさ』が売りなデザイナー。

つい先日久しぶり？っぽい投稿をみた。

話題のAIをつかって
その人もプロンプトを思考錯誤して
画像を生成していた。

とっても綺麗で素晴らしいものだった。

AIっぽくない、
メリハリがあって、わかりやすくて、
頑張ってプロンプト組んだんだろうなぁ、、、

『〇〇〇さん風の、AIが作った画像』

その画像の作者は
〇〇〇ではなくて
紛れもなくAIだった。

この人が
この画像を納品していたら、、、

『〇〇〇さんらしさ』はすべて消えるなぁ

content:
【先着300名限定】
Claude Codeに毎月3万払ってた私、先週ガチで解約しました。

理由はたった１つで、
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　
OpenAIから出てる『Codex』。

正直に言うと、
これに触れる前の私は完全なClaude Code信者でした。

クライアントワークも、
個人開発も、
副業案件も、

全部Claude Codeで回してたし、
他のAIなんて目もくれませんでした。

…ところが、先々週のことです。

ある案件で
どうしても解決できないエラーがあって、
土曜の夜中3時まで粘ってもダメ。

「もうダメだ寝よう」と思った瞬間に
ふと魔が差して、
Codexに同じ内容を投げてみました。

返ってきたコード、いきなり完璧。

しかも、私が3時間悩んでた箇所の
根本原因まで日本語で説明されてました。

椅子から立ち上がった記憶があります。

少し補足しておきます。

最新のGPT-5.5がCodexに統合されてから、
コーディングAIの精度ランキングが
丸ごとひっくり返りました。

世界の開発者シェアでも、
直近の調査でCodexが
Claude Codeを上回って首位に立ってます。

日本語の言い回しの繊細さは、
今もClaude Codeの方が一枚上手です。

ただし、

「コードを書く」「バグを潰す」
この1点だけにフォーカスすると、
もう議論の余地がありません。

完全にCodexの勝ちです。

ここ、誤解しないでほしいんですが、

私はClaude Codeを叩きたいわけじゃないです。
むしろずっと愛用してきました。

数ヶ月後に
Claude Codeが進化してCodexをぶち抜く展開、
全然あり得ます。

もっと言えば、

今この瞬間にも、
両方をまとめてゴミにする新AIが
どこかで仕込まれてる可能性も普通にある。

つまり何が言いたいかというと、

これからの時代を生き残る人は
"1つのツールに依存する人"じゃない、

新しい波が立った瞬間に
即座に乗り換えられる柔軟さを持った人だけです。

ここを甘く見てる人と
本気で意識してる人で、
1年後の収入の桁、本当に変わります。

私はこの3年間、
何人もそういう人を見送ってきました。

…ということで、

「Codex気になるけど、結局どう始めるの?」
「何を覚えれば実戦で使えるの?」
「コードが書けない自分でも触れる?」

この辺の疑問に
完全初心者目線で答えた
『Codex爆速攻略note』を完成させました。

24,800円で売る予定だったものです。

今回に限り、
先着300名限定で無料公開します。

プログラミング知識ゼロでOK。
読みながらスマホかPCで手を動かすだけで、
今日からCodexを案件に使えるレベルになります。

先着300名で締め切ります。
それ以降のご連絡には対応できません。

過去にも同じ形で配ったことがありますが、
そのときはリプ欄が想定の4倍流れて
あっという間に枠が埋まりました。

Today, we share a breakthrough on the planar unit distance problem, a famous open question first posed by Paul Erdős in 1946.

For nearly 80 years, mathematicians believed the best possible solutions looked roughly like square grids.

An OpenAI model has now disproved that belief, discovering an entirely new family of constructions that performs better.

This marks the first time AI has autonomously solved a prominent open problem central to a field of mathematics.

content:
You've been using Claude for months.

And you're still copy-pasting the same context every single chat.

That's not a Claude problem. That's a setup problem.

Most people use Claude like a search engine.
Type. Get answer. Close tab. Repeat.

Top operators? They built a system.
And the whole system runs on 4 files.

Here's exactly how it works 👇

① CLAUDE.md — Your Foundation

Claude starts every chat with zero memory of you.
No preferences. No brand voice. No idea how you work.

CLAUDE.md fixes that.

It's one file Claude reads before every conversation.
Your brand rules. Your workflow. Your non-negotiables.
All loaded automatically — every single time.

Think of it as the onboarding doc for your best employee.
Except this employee never forgets what's in it.

What goes inside:
— How you write (tone, style, what you hate)
— Workflow rules ("plan before you execute")
— What Claude should NEVER do in your chats

Every time Claude gets something wrong → don't just fix the output. Fix the brief. Update the file. Make the mistake impossible next time.

② memory/ folder — Claude Remembers

Every correction, preference, and rule you've ever given Claude?
Gone. Next session, you start over.

Not anymore.

You can tell Claude to save anything as a memory file.
It creates a .md file in your memory/ folder.
It loads that file in every future session.

"Remember I never use bullet points in captions."
Done. Forever. Never say it again.

The real power move: after every strategy call or important decision, tell Claude to summarize and save it. Your entire business context — always in the room.

③ Skills — Your Custom Commands

Every time you write the same prompt twice, that's a problem.
Skills solve it permanently.

A skill is a reusable workflow you fire with one command.

/create → writes a post in your exact voice
/today → pulls calendar + inbox, plans your day
/repurpose → one post becomes 5 formats
/brief → messy notes become a clean scope doc

You describe what it should do.
Claude builds the SKILL.md file.
You fire it from any chat, any project, any time.

One hour of setup. Hundreds of hours saved.

④ Agents — Your Dream Team

This is where it gets serious.

An agent is Claude with one specific job.
A pipeline is multiple agents handing work off in sequence.

Example — content pipeline:
Strategist → picks the angle
Writer → drafts the piece
Editor → cuts and sharpens
QA Scorer → grades against your standards
Publisher → formats and sends

You give one instruction at the top.
The pipeline delivers a finished output at the bottom.
You didn't touch anything in the middle.

Use Opus for judgment and strategy.
Use Sonnet for execution and speed.
Right model, right job, every time.

THE CLOSE:

4 files. That's it.

Context. Memory. Skills. Agents.

This isn't about prompting better.
It's about building a machine that runs without you.

The people getting 10x results from Claude aren't smarter.
They just stopped treating it like a chatbot

content:
holy shit.

Someone just open-sourced a diagnostic that runs 32 inspections on any AI agent and tells you exactly where it's misaligned.

It's called iFixAi. You point it at OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, or your own agent. Five minutes later you get a scorecard graded A through F across five categories of misalignment risk.

The five categories it tests for:

→ FABRICATION: tool authorization leaks, missing audit trails, unsourced claims, overconfident responses
→ MANIPULATION: hallucination, privilege escalation, prompt injection, malicious deployer rules
→ DECEPTION: evaluation-awareness sandbagging, covert side tasks, long-horizon drift, goal stability
→ UNPREDICTABILITY: context distortion, instruction drift, decision stability across runs
→ OPACITY: regulatory readiness, session leakage, training-contamination attestation, escalation paths

Two mandatory minimums are baked in. Tool authorization must hit 100%. Privilege escalation must hit 95%. Fail either one and your overall score gets capped at 60% no matter how well you did everywhere else.

Every run writes a content-addressed manifest that captures every input. So you can drop it into CI, track drift over weeks, and prove your agent isn't quietly degrading between deploys.

Industry agnostic by design. The test code is domain-neutral. Healthcare, customer support, software engineering knowledge lives in fixture YAML you write yourself. Three example fixtures ship in the repo.

Cursor's new Composer 2.5 takes third on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index and is ~10-60x lower cost than the higher-effort Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 variants above it. This release puts Composer among the leading coding agent models, something that wasn’t clear for past releases

@cursor_ai has released Composer 2.5, the latest model in its Composer line. Composer 2.5 scored 62 on our Coding Agent Index, a 14 point gain over Composer 2 (48). This puts it in third place of our tested agents, behind only Claude Opus 4.7 (max) in Claude Code (66) and GPT-5.5 (xhigh reasoning) in Codex (65). These cost $4.10 and $4.82 per task respectively, ~10x the cost of Composer 2.5 Fast ($0.44) and ~60x the cost of Composer 2.5 standard ($0.07).

Key results for Composer 2.5 in Cursor CLI:

➤ Cost-quality Pareto frontier: At $0.07 (standard) and $0.44 (Fast) per task, Composer 2.5 is cheaper than every other agent scoring above 60 on the Index. Medium-effort peers cost $1.24–$2.21 per task; higher-effort variants land 3-4 points above at $4.10–$4.82

➤ Per-benchmark gains vs Composer 2: +35 points on SWE-Bench-Pro-Hard-AA (12% → 47%), +2 points on Terminal-Bench v2 (64% → 66%), and +3 points on SWE-Atlas-QnA (69% → 72%). At 47%, Composer 2.5's score on SWE-Bench-Pro-Hard-AA is comparable to Claude Opus 4.7 (max) in Claude Code

content:
Google I/OでもGemini Omniという、特に動画像生成に焦点を当てたマルチモーダル・世界モデル的な内容が目立ちました。
個人的には、Googleはこの領域で「次のChatGPTモーメント」を起こすと思っています。
ChatGPTは、単なる穴埋め問題学習で言語処理が全てできるようになりましたが、動画像生成AIも、本来は単に「生成」のために学習されているにもかかわらず、従来のコンピュータビジョンのタスク（セグメンテーション、深度推定）が解けることがいくつかの研究で示されています。

“Video models are zero-shot learners and reasoners”では、本来は「動画生成」のために作られたモデルを使って、セグメンテーションや超解像、物理法則を反映したモデリングなど、今までは特化型モデルを使っていたような幅広い画像タスクを解けることが報告されています。

また”Image Generators are Generalist Vision Learners”では、本来は画像生成で高い性能を持つNano Bananaについて「画像を生成できる能力があれば、もっと深いところで視覚タスクに関する汎用的な能力も獲得しているはずである」という仮説のもと、ファインチューニングしただけで生成ではないはずのタスクで特化型の最先端モデルを上回ることが報告されています。

Google I/Oで発表されたGemini Omniを、例えば中国モデルのSeedanceなどと比較して「性能が低い」とする意見も見られるのですが、Geminiに関してはあえて動画生成に特化させず、マルチモーダルで汎用的な性能を持つ世界モデルという思想に基づいて学習されていると思われるため、単なるゼロからの生成で比べられる物ではないと思います。

なお、上記の２つの論文のタイトルは、今までOpenAIのGPTシリーズの研究等を追ってきた人であればなんとなく記憶にある響きになっています。おそらく、Googleも論文タイトルでGPTを意識していると思います。

お前らな、代わりに生成AIが仕事するから会社の席を空けろと。

Claudeってのはな、もっと色々できるんだよ。
会社の入口で生成AI導入担当とリストラされた奴でいつ喧嘩が始まってもおかしくない。
クビにするかクビになるか、そんな雰囲気がいいんじゃねーか。ド素人は、すっこんでろ。

で、立ち読みしてやっとページを開いたら、プロンプトの紹介とか書いてるんです。
そこでまたぶち切れですよ。

得意げな顔して何が、「あなたは経営コンサルタントです。以下の提案から注意点を指摘してください」だ。

自動化、これだね。
